__README: Pre-split variant-to-value baseline for the exit-code classification tables.
Recovered from commit 7adaea627e9de2f0d1e90780c9c9997aea72d3f6 — the frozen base of WP-10, the last revision at
which every `ClassifyExitCode` / `ClassifyErrorKind` impl still lived inside
`ocx_lib` and every match over an OCX-owned error enum was total.
WHY THIS MUST NEVER BE REGENERATED FROM THE CURRENT TREE:
This file exists to pin the mapping from each error variant to the exit code
and `kind_detail` string `ocx` emitted BEFORE the classification moved out of
the library crates. Regenerating it from HEAD would re-baseline the exact
thing it exists to detect, and the tests reading it would then pass by
construction. A drift against this file is a finding, never a reason to
refresh the file.
A vocabulary census cannot replace it. At the base revision 92 string-valued
`kind_detail` arms produce only 83 distinct strings, so many-to-one is already
normal and a variant newly collapsing onto an existing string is invisible to
any count of distinct literals. Only the variant-to-value pair catches it.
`ocx` exit codes are a published interface that scripts branch on with
`case $?`, and `kind_detail` is the frozen `error.detail` vocabulary of the
JSON error envelope (contract C-S1-1). Both are observable; neither may move
under a structural refactor.
Consumed by the per-impl table tests in `crates/ocx_cli/src/exit/`. Each row is
one match arm: `pattern` is the arm's left-hand side as written at the base
revision, `value` its right-hand side, `source` the file:line it came from.
`_` as a pattern is a wildcard arm — there were exactly 4 at the base revision.
SECOND RECOVERY (WP-43, 355 -> 370 arms). The first extractor split each line
on `=>` without joining an arm whose right-hand side opened a block, so every
`... => {` arm was discarded rather than recorded. 15 arms were missing, and
two of them were the only guard their impl had:
`ManagedConfigPublishError::classify`'s `ExtraCaCertsInvalid | ExtraCaCertsNotUtf8`
(65) and `PublishGateError::classify`'s `DependencyPinnedToIndex |
AnyPinNotAdvertisedAsAny` (65) — both survived a mutation with the whole
`cargo test -p ocx --lib` run byte-identical. The 15 were re-read from
7adaea62 itself, never from HEAD, joining each block arm to its matching `}`
and recording the inside; the consumer's `arms_in` joins the same way, so a
block arm and the one-line arm it was reflowed from compare equal. The rule
against regenerating from the current tree is unchanged and applies to these
rows exactly as it does to the first 355.
THIRD RECOVERY (WP-43, 370 -> 372 arms). Both earlier recoveries read the
base revision with a line scanner, and a line scanner cannot read Rust. It
split every body line on `=>`, so a pattern spanning several lines became
several rows and a value spanning several lines was cut at its first line.
49 of the 370 rows were wrong in one of five ways, all of which read as
coverage:
31  a trailing fragment of a multi-line `|` alternation recorded as if it
were a whole arm — `| Self::ExtractionCapExceeded { .. }` is not a
pattern any `match` contains, and the head of its alternation was lost
4  the closing line of a multi-line pattern recorded as the pattern, so
the two `KeyUnreadable`/`KeyMalformed` carve-outs in verify/error.rs
were pinned as `})`
3  a value cut at the brace that opens it — `match inner {`
1  a value cut to its first line — `ProjectErrorKind::RegistryUnreachable`
was pinned as `source` where the arm is a five-line downcast chain
10  a block-form arm stored without the braces the second recovery stripped
None of the five reddened, because the consumer scanned the relocated tree
the same broken way: both sides agreed on the same wrong reading, which is
the shape of a check that asserts the code equals itself.
Re-extracted from 7adaea62 with a `syn` parse — the impl, its functions, its
match arms and each arm’s guard read as syntax, never as text. Every row here
is one real arm: 321 are the committed row kept verbatim, 51 are new or
corrected. The rule against regenerating from the *current* tree is unchanged
and was not broken to do this: the source was the base revision, checked out
from git, exactly as for the first two recoveries.
DEC-46 (2026-09-18): `func` and `match_id` added to every row. This is a
RESOLUTION change at an UNCHANGED revision, not a re-freeze — the arms, their
patterns, their values and their sources are byte-identical to what was
recovered, and the enrichment is a join on `source`, which is a bijection over
all 372 rows. It was derived by running the pin's own `arms_in` over the
7adaea62 sources, which reproduced all rows with zero missing, zero extra and
zero type or trait disagreement; a second extractor was deliberately not used.
The premise DEC-43 rests on is untouched: the revision is still 7adaea62, so a
relocation row's job is still to map today's spelling back to this one.
WHY THE FINER KEY: the comparison keyed on (type, trait, pattern), which merged
372 arms into 358 keys and compared by MEMBERSHIP — asking whether the
baseline's value was among the candidates rather than whether it WAS the value.
Two arms of one impl matched in different functions therefore satisfied each
other. With func and match_id the 372 arms are 372 keys, and the comparison is
equality.
`frozen_columns_sha256` is sha256 over the five columns that existed before
DEC-46 — type, trait, pattern, value, source — tab-joined, newline-terminated,
in file order. It was computed from the FROZEN file and is checked by
`the_enrichment_added_columns_and_changed_no_frozen_value`. A bijection on the
join key says nothing about what a writer does to values, so the claim that
the enrichment added columns and altered no exit code is a property the tool
checks rather than a sentence in a commit message.
